classification.difficultyReason: Choose readable points or rise-and-run intervals on each graph, calculate signed gradients, and apply the explicitly requested product test for perpendicularity.

content.prompt: By finding the product of the gradients, show that each pair of lines are perpendicular.

spec.description: Unit square grid from −4 to 4 with positive arrowed axes and numeric origin label. Blue falls through (−4,4), (−2,1) and (0,−2). Red rises through (−4,−1), crossing the horizontal axis at −2.5 and the vertical axis between 1 and 2.

answer.worked:
For the red line, a run of $3$ corresponds to a rise of $2$.
$$\begin{align*}m_{\text{blue}}&=\frac{-2-1}{0-(-2)}\\&=-\frac32\\m_{\text{red}}&=\frac23\\m_{\text{blue}}\times m_{\text{red}}&=\left(-\frac32\right)\left(\frac23\right)\\&=-1\end{align*}$$
The lines are perpendicular.
